questions.question_text_en: Among the agencies of justice, the ones where elders play a vital role are
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: supreme courts

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: traditional courts

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: conventional courts

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: international courts

explanation.solution_text_en: Traditional courts and indigenous dispute-resolution institutions commonly rely on respected community elders who know local customs and social norms. This distinguishes them from the formal hierarchy of conventional courts.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Understanding Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 10 - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution

secondary_curriculum_links: Grade 10 - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is the principal duty of tax payers?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The current curriculum states the duty more directly as paying the lawful tax liability. Horizontal and vertical equity are mainly principles for designing and administering a fair tax system, so none of the choices states the principal duty perfectly.  ESSLCE / EUEE Civics and Ethical Education | 2014/15 E.C. | Curriculum-Aligned Study Guide
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Make sure the imposed tax is based on their ability to pay.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Fulfill their duty with regard to the action of government.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: To pay tax based on horizontal and vertical principle.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To pay the same amount of tax for different amount of income.

explanation.solution_text_en: The basic duty of a taxpayer is to pay the tax legally due. Among the listed choices, C is the closest because horizontal and vertical equity are principles used to make tax burdens fair across people with similar or different ability to pay.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains clearly the relationship between a constitution and other laws?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A constitution is relatively permanent while other laws are often subject to change.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The constitution contains detailed laws and principles while other laws are general.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Both the constitution and other laws are made by parliament.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Other laws are formulated with much more care compared to the constitution.

explanation.solution_text_en: A constitution is the supreme and relatively stable legal framework of the state, while ordinary laws are made and changed within that framework. Ordinary laws must conform to the constitution.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: Among the following, which one makes voluntary associations distinct from other organizations? They are
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: organized to achieve public well-being.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: established as business firms.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: dependent on government.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: mainly political association.

explanation.solution_text_en: Voluntary associations are formed by people who freely organize around shared social or community goals. Their defining purpose is not profit or dependence on government, but collective action for common or public interests.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following obligations of citizens is instrumental in solving conflict?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: Negotiation is a conflict-resolution method rather than, by itself, a general legal obligation of citizenship. It is nevertheless the only option directly connected with solving conflict.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Paying tax

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Negotiation

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Assimilation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Avoiding differences

explanation.solution_text_en: Negotiation is a peaceful conflict-resolution method in which parties communicate directly to seek an acceptable settlement. It helps citizens manage disagreements without violence.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution Mechanisms

questions.question_text_en: Respecting the constitution of a country and abiding by it is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a moral obligation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a legal obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a cultural obligation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: an economic obligation

explanation.solution_text_en: A constitution is the supreme law of the country. Citizens and public officials are legally required to respect and act in accordance with it.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: The people of Konso in South western Ethiopia protected the beautiful Konso land scape from environmental damage for centuries. Preservation of the environment in this way contributes to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: eco-tourism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: carbon emission

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: deforestation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: global warming

explanation.solution_text_en: Protecting a distinctive cultural landscape and its environment can support eco-tourism because visitors are attracted by well-preserved natural and cultural heritage. Deforestation, carbon emissions and global warming are environmental harms, not benefits of preservation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 8: Economy, Environment and Climate Change

secondary_curriculum_links: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 8: Economy, Environment and Climate Change

questions.question_text_en: Maintaining labour discipline in a profession is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: unfair

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: ethical

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: wastage

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: unnecessary

explanation.solution_text_en: Labour discipline - punctuality, responsibility, reliability and proper use of work time and resources - is part of ethical conduct at the workplace.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a strategy devised by the Ethiopian government to enhance the economic development of the country?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Dependency on goods from other countries

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Promoting industrialization before agriculture

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Creation of consumer society

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Agricultural Development Led Industrialization

explanation.solution_text_en: Agricultural Development Led Industrialization (ADLI) was a major Ethiopian development strategy that emphasized agricultural growth as a basis for broader industrialization. Current Grade 12 economics treats such earlier strategies as part of Ethiopia's macroeconomic reform history.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 7: Macroeconomic Reforms in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following characterizes a person who has a proper perception about his/her self?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Having an attitude of superiority

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Self-awareness

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Exaggerating one's weakness

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Being dominated by others

explanation.solution_text_en: Proper self-perception begins with self-awareness: realistically recognizing one's strengths, weaknesses, feelings and capabilities. Superiority, exaggerating weakness or being dominated by others are distorted forms of self-perception.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7: Ethical Values; Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Among the following, which one is true about the impact of dependency on nations' Dependency
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: limits the potential of poor countries for sustainable growth.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: creates a balanced relationship between rich and poor countries.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: provides opportunities for economic growth for poor countries.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: contributes to technology transfer from rich countries to poor ones.

explanation.solution_text_en: Harmful dependency can weaken domestic capacity, autonomy and incentives to build sustainable productive systems. That can limit long-term growth even when outside support is useful in some circumstances.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6: Economic Development; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: In Equb, the member who collects money at the end among the members is considered to have
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: borrowed

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: received a dividend

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: been insured

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: saved

explanation.solution_text_en: Equb is a rotating saving arrangement. A member who receives the pooled contribution at the end has effectively accumulated savings through repeated contributions over the cycle.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Consumption, Saving and Investment; indigenous saving practices

questions.question_text_en: Among the following, one is an indicator of the enabling condition which saving creates for development
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Raising funds from depositors meant for investment

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Collecting money from depositors and spending it

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Keeping money in banks indefinitely

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Transferring depositors' money abroad

explanation.solution_text_en: Saving supports development when financial institutions mobilize deposits and channel them into investment. Merely holding or spending deposits does not create the same productive financing role.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Consumption, Saving and Investment; Unit 5: Trade and Finance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following makes part of cooperation among different countries?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Cooperation is established only during war times.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Countries cooperate for reasonable use of natural and social resources.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Countries cooperate to mismanage nature when there is no common objectives to achieve.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Cooperation results when there is no common objectives to achieve.

explanation.solution_text_en: International cooperation allows countries to manage shared natural and social resources, solve cross-border problems and pursue common goals. Cooperation is not limited to war and requires shared objectives.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa

questions.question_text_en: A thought process which contributes to the attainment of objective judgment is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: objectivity

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: ignorance

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: reasoning

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: subjectivity

explanation.solution_text_en: Reasoning is the process of examining information and relationships in order to reach justified conclusions. It supports objectivity by reducing decisions based only on bias or personal preference.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: In due process of conflict resolution and maintaining order and security, the observance of rule of law can be checked by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: habeas corpus, nonpartisan trial and presumption of innocence.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: partial tribunal of courts in dealing with cases.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the burden of the defendant to prove his/her innocence.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the possibility of double jeopardy in exceptional cases.

explanation.solution_text_en: Habeas corpus, impartial trial and the presumption of innocence are core procedural safeguards. They help ensure that state power is exercised according to law and that accused persons receive due process.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 3 & 6: Good Governance; Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is not a necessary requirement for the acceptability, universal applicability of laws?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Non-violating other values of cultural groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Creating blur of meanings and ambiguity.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Easy to understand and without jargon expressions.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Practicality and possibility to follow within the power of humanity.

explanation.solution_text_en: For laws to be acceptable and broadly applicable, they should be clear, understandable, practical and compatible with fundamental rights and legitimate values. Deliberately creating ambiguity works against those requirements.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: For nations like Ethiopia, diversity is one of the values as well as challenges of national unity. When people aspire to develop their own cultures, maintaining equality and recognition of languages, religions, and other cultural traits contributes to national unity. But against this norm, there are individuals or groups who have a tendency to consider their own identities are good and superior to others. Furthermore, such tendencies may lead into assumption that others are inferior and enemies. Such tendency is known as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: ethnocentrism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: eurocentrism

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: multiculturalism

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: accommodative

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other groups by the standards of one's own group and to regard one's own culture or identity as superior. That can undermine equality and national unity in a diverse society.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6: Multiculturalism; National Unity through Diversity

questions.question_text_en: Which action demonstrates tolerance of diversity?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Imposing your ideas on others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Exercising empathy for others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Isolating yourself from people who have different viewpoints

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Passively listening others' viewpoints

explanation.solution_text_en: Tolerance involves trying to understand people whose beliefs or identities differ from one's own. Empathy supports respectful coexistence, while imposing views or isolating oneself works against tolerance.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about rule of law, constitution and constitutionalism?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: D is the closest option, but rule of law is more than citizens simply obeying commands of law; it also requires lawful, accountable and non-arbitrary government.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The existence of written constitutions is the requirement for constitutionalism and rule of law.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Constitutionalism is an aspect of government officials to advance their interests in the name of the constitution.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Constitutionalism cannot be developed in the absence of written constitutions since there are no guidelines for constitutionalism.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Constitutionalism and rule of law are almost synonymous that people abide by the command of the laws of the land.

explanation.solution_text_en: Rule of law and constitutionalism are closely related because both reject arbitrary rule and require government and citizens to act within a lawful constitutional framework. Constitutionalism, however, also specifically emphasizes limiting government power through constitutional principles.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: What can be generalized about the different struggles of the people of Ethiopian against autocratic rulers?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The Ethiopian movement was initiated by the international influences than the internal political, social and economic realities.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: They were intended to self-determination and carry secessionist objectives of elites.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Many of them were peasant rebellions against the increment of taxes, corruption, and maladministration by the central government.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The outbreak of the 1974 Revolution was the first incident in the history of Ethiopia that challenged the status quo of the emperor.

explanation.solution_text_en: Many major challenges to centralized autocratic rule in modern Ethiopian history included peasant uprisings linked to taxation, land grievances, corruption and maladministration. The 1974 Revolution was therefore not the first challenge to imperial authority.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Units 3 & 6: Ethiopia, mid-19th century to 1941; Ethiopia 1941-1991

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements explains the major characteristic feature of a democratic system?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A democratic system should have a constitution given by an elected political party

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: In a democratic system citizens may be partially treated

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A democratic system compromises the rights of thought, opinion and expression

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A democratic system demands active participation of all citizens

explanation.solution_text_en: Meaningful democracy depends on active and informed citizen participation, including voting, discussion, association and engagement in public affairs. Democratic systems also protect thought, opinion and expression.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is true about the nature and structure of the Ethiopian state?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethiopia has now an ethno linguistic federal state structure

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: During the Derg regime, power was shared between the central and provincial governments

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Under Emperor Haile Selassie, Ethiopia was an absolutist federal state

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: In its long history, Ethiopia has similar state structure

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE is a federal state whose constituent units are substantially organized around Nations, Nationalities and Peoples and their territories. Earlier imperial and Derg governments were much more centralized or unitary.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; Grade 12 History - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements explains best the principle of the Ethiopian foreign policy?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's foreign policy aims at getting economic aid from developed capitalist countries

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It advances interference in the internal affairs of small neighboring countries

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It promotes mutual economic development

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It compromises the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity

explanation.solution_text_en: A central principle of peaceful foreign relations is cooperation based on mutual benefit, including trade and development. Foreign policy should also protect national sovereignty and avoid unlawful interference in other states.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa

questions.question_text_en: One of the following statements is correct about the history of constitution in Ethiopia?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The item is not cleanly single-answer. Historical sources also show that the 1987 Constitution recognized nationalities and provided some related rights/autonomy, so option A can be defended depending on wording. B is retained as the clearest answer to the statement as written.  ESSLCE / EUEE Civics and Ethical Education | 2014/15 E.C. | Curriculum-Aligned Study Guide
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The 1987 Constitution contains provisions about the rights of nations, nationalities and peoples

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The 1955 Revised Constitution asserted citizens' freedom of expression

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The 1931 Constitution made the king a constitutional monarch

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The 1995 Constitution fully addresses the political, economic and social rights of citizens

explanation.solution_text_en: The 1955 Revised Constitution expressly recognized freedom of speech and of the press, although the practical protection of such rights was limited. This makes B a clearly supportable historical statement.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 12 History - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: Unlike unlimited government, a limited government
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: exercises power without taking into account the interests of citizens

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: does not take into account public opinion

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: simply take major policy measures without consulting citizens

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: institutionalizes and exercises accountability to the people

explanation.solution_text_en: Limited government operates under constitutional and legal restraints and is accountable to the public. Unlimited government, by contrast, concentrates power without effective checks or responsibility to citizens.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements explains the concept of gender equality in contemporary Ethiopia? It refers to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: equality of men and women to enjoy equal opportunity

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: safeguarding the rights and interest of women only

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: empowering women to dominate men

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: limiting the power of men vis-à-vis women

explanation.solution_text_en: Gender equality means women and men should enjoy equal rights, dignity and opportunities. It does not mean replacing one form of domination with another.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Equal access in social services is important because
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: it provides all citizens equal living standards

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: it creates the feeling of belonging and achievement among all citizens

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: it creates identical distribution of resources among citizens

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: it eliminates income disparity among citizens

explanation.solution_text_en: Fair access to education, health and other social services strengthens inclusion and gives citizens a sense that they belong to and benefit from the political community. Equality does not require identical outcomes for everyone.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 3 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements explains the history of taxation in Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The tax systems of monarchs was opposed by the peasants

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ethiopia had an effective and efficient system of tax collection

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: In Ethiopia taxation started in the twentieth century

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: All eligible tax payers are paying their share

explanation.solution_text_en: Historically, burdensome taxation and abuses in collection contributed to peasant grievances and rebellions in different periods of Ethiopian history. Taxation existed long before the twentieth century.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Units 3 & 6; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: Which part of the society should pay tax?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The question and answer choices appear corrupted or mismatched. The current curriculum answer is that all persons and entities meeting the legal tax base/threshold should pay the taxes required by law; none of the choices states this correctly.  ESSLCE / EUEE Civics and Ethical Education | 2014/15 E.C. | Curriculum-Aligned Study Guide
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: being self-confident and make good decisions about their own lives

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Corrupt officials who embezzle public money

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Big businessmen who gets loans from the banks

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: assertive and proactive and endorse their own views regardless of the views from others

explanation.solution_text_en: People and businesses whose taxable income or transactions fall within the law should pay tax. Of the supplied options, C is the only one that refers to an income-earning business group, but bank borrowing is not what creates tax liability.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be a personal quality of a dedicated Ethiopian citizen?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Showing concern and devotion to Ethiopia's sovereignty

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Insulting Ethiopia's official flag

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Becoming a legal member of the Ethiopian state

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Disseminating unverified news from unauthorized sources

explanation.solution_text_en: A dedicated citizen shows concern for the country's sovereignty, constitutional order and common good. Insulting national symbols or spreading unverified information does not demonstrate responsible citizenship.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Grade 9 - Unit 2

questions.question_text_en: Citizens can fight backwardness and poverty within the limits of their capacity through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: increasing the size of their family

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: hard working in businesses they engaged

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: praying for a windfall fortune

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: accepting poverty as God given

explanation.solution_text_en: Industrious and productive work is a direct way citizens can contribute to overcoming poverty and backwardness. Development requires effort, skills and productive activity rather than passivity or fatalism.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6: Economic Development; Grade 10 Citizenship - Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: An active young Ethiopian citizen can take part in voluntary activity through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: assisting persons with illness for payments

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: establishing a small scale enterprise to benefit oneself

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: joining profit making organizations which sales commodities to society

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: giving free service to aging citizens

explanation.solution_text_en: Voluntary activity is service freely given for the benefit of others without requiring payment. Providing unpaid help to older citizens is therefore the clearest example.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Civic participation; Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Unlike personal responsibility, group responsibility entails you to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: do for your own good

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: play some roles in your community

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: contribute to the wellbeing of your family

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: enjoy individual rights stated in the constitution

explanation.solution_text_en: Group responsibility concerns duties that arise from membership in a community or organization. Playing a constructive role in the community is broader than acting only for personal benefit.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values; Grade 10 - Unit 1

questions.question_text_en: One of the following actions demonstrates citizen's responsibility in their every walk of life?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Showing disrespect to the privacy of others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Promoting personal interests at the expense of social interests

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Behaving in a proper way under any circumstances

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Violating the values and norms of the society

explanation.solution_text_en: Responsible citizenship requires ethical conduct across everyday situations, including respect for others, social norms and lawful responsibilities. Promoting private interest at the expense of others contradicts that responsibility.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Citizens can protect natural resources and cultural heritages through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: keeping the resources out of the reach of mankind

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: using the resources fully and then replacing them by new similar ones

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: using the resources in a responsible way

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: replacing cultural heritages by modern industrial products

explanation.solution_text_en: Natural resources and cultural heritage are best protected through responsible, sustainable use and conservation. Protection does not require making them completely inaccessible or replacing heritage with modern products.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: In which economic system an individual can produce and sell the goods and services that earn him/her a good reward?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Planned economic system

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Mixed economic system

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Command economic system

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Free market economic system

explanation.solution_text_en: A free-market system gives private individuals broad freedom to own resources, produce goods and services, and sell them in markets in pursuit of profit, subject to law and regulation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - economic systems and market structures

questions.question_text_en: Good work ethics refers to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: integrity at work place

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: power to influence other fellow workers

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: lack of reliability at work place

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: inappropriate use of resources

explanation.solution_text_en: Integrity at the workplace means honesty, reliability and consistency between ethical standards and behavior. It is a central part of good work ethics.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be considered as consequence of dependency?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: "Feeling of melancholy" is not a standard curriculum term for dependency. It is simply the closest negative consequence among the supplied choices.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Dependable

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Feeling of melancholy

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Effectiveness at work

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Self-esteem

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency can undermine confidence and create discouragement or a sense of helplessness. The other listed traits - effectiveness and self-esteem - are generally associated with self-reliance rather than dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7; Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: The first step to combat against dependency should be
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: to become self-reliant

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: negotiating with the influencing bodies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: creating a buffer zone around yourself

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: to be aware of self-weaknesses

explanation.solution_text_en: A useful first step in reducing dependency is honest self-awareness: identifying weaknesses, needs and the causes of dependence. That awareness helps a person plan how to build capacity and become more self-reliant.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following characterizes best the practice of tax evasion?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is a fraud where people do not reveal their total income or pay the approximate tax

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It is an unnecessary increment in the amount of tax the sake of empowering leaders

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is a government imposition of higher amount of tax to demote dangerous businesses

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is a government initiated tax deduction to attract people into favored types of businesses

explanation.solution_text_en: Tax evasion is the illegal concealment or misrepresentation of taxable income, transactions or property in order to reduce tax liability. It is different from lawful tax planning or avoidance.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is wrong about tax avoidance?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is the act of changing one's business to one that pays less tax

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It can be done when one's business into sectors favored by the government which are charged less taxes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is done when business men/women are smart enough to decide the type of their business

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is an implicit and illegal practice that people feel themselves from tax

explanation.solution_text_en: Tax avoidance generally refers to arranging activities within the law to reduce tax liability, while tax evasion is illegal concealment or fraud. Therefore describing tax avoidance as an illegal practice is the incorrect statement.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is wrong about Ethiopia's global or continental international contributions?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: Option A is also awkward because being a borrower/customer of international financial institutions is not normally described as an international "contribution." B is the clearly false historical claim as written.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's being an exemplary customer of international development funds and monetary aid of IMF and World Bank

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's being an exemplary defender of colonialism, African independence and establishment of the Organization of African Unity

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's being a member of the League of Nations founded in 1920 to maintain global peace and cooperation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's participation in regional and international peacekeeping activities in South Korea, Congo, Rwanda, Burundi and others

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethiopia is historically associated with resistance to colonial domination and support for African independence and Pan-African cooperation, not with defending colonialism. It also joined the League of Nations and has participated in international peacekeeping.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Units 5 & 7: Global developments; Africa since the 1960s

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statement is true about the similarity between the House of Federation and House of People's Representative?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Quorum of meetings of the two houses is the attendance of more than half of members of each house.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Members of the two houses is represented by regional state council.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Members of the two houses is accountable for the leading party.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Every nation, nationality and peoples of Ethiopia at least represented by one member of the two houses.

explanation.solution_text_en: Both federal houses require a majority of their members for a quorum under their governing rules/constitutional framework. The two houses differ in how members are chosen and whom they directly represent.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE constitutional institutions

questions.question_text_en: Which one is wrong about the benefits of responsible citizens?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: There are prescribed social and personal responsibilities prioritized according to our place in the society and fulfilling them entail benefits for all.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: If persons are not willing to participate in wars of protecting their own nation, they are deprived of their rights regardless of their reasons.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: By shouldering one's responsibility, one can develop self-esteem and self-belief.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: For any responsibility executed properly and successfully, there is reciprocal reward, implicit or explicit.

explanation.solution_text_en: Fundamental rights are not automatically lost merely because a person does not participate in war, especially regardless of the person's lawful reasons. Responsible conduct can bring personal and social benefits, but rights remain constitutionally protected.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 6 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Costs of shouldering and executing one's responsibilities include all except
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: slaughtering one's close families for national interest.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: sacrificing private interests.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: sacrificing their own lives.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: paying taxes and financial contributions from one's own incomes.

explanation.solution_text_en: Civic responsibility can involve legitimate sacrifice of time, money, private interests and, in extreme lawful circumstances, personal risk. Killing close family members is not a legitimate civic responsibility.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which can be a false statement about HIV/AIDS and related pandemics at the international level?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: HIV/AIDS is a unique phenomenon that highly affects poor countries in comparison with rich countries.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Such pandemics affect all indiscriminately regardless of differences in color, sex, religion or occupation.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Diseases like HIV/AIDS may have positive consequences in combating poverty in poor countries by facilitating international aid.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Fighting diseases like HIV/AIDS demands intergovernmental cooperation, engagement of international organizations and humanitarian aid.

explanation.solution_text_en: A pandemic is a public-health and development problem, not a beneficial poverty-reduction mechanism. International aid can help affected societies, but the disease itself cannot be treated as a positive route to reducing poverty.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: What is the importance of planning on production and consumption? It enables
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: us to understand what we want and the resources available

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: mankind to use natural resources as they wish

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: factories to emit unhealthy gases

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: us to consume all the resources and money we have

explanation.solution_text_en: Planning compares goals and wants with available resources before production or consumption decisions are made. This supports efficient, responsible use of money and natural resources.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Grade 11 Economics - Consumption and Saving

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following affects the world of work negatively?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: In a work environment, where the social interaction is strong people tend to like their work and can be satisfied with it.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The existence of ethical standards which guide the professional responsibilities of workers assist the proper functioning of their jobs.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Following certain ethical standards that prohibit the offence of co-workers, productivity of workers increase.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: In a workplace where the worker is relationship with others is not harmonious, the level of job satisfaction declines.

explanation.solution_text_en: Poor interpersonal relationships and unresolved conflict at work reduce satisfaction and can harm productivity. Ethical standards and positive social interaction usually support a healthier work environment.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Self-reliant persons are known by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: being self-confident and make good decisions about their own lives.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: self-awareness of their own strength and weaknesses to effectively win others.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: strength and effort to support themselves without the need of help from others.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: assertive and proactive and endorse their own views regardless of the views from others.

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-reliance means developing the capacity to support oneself and make responsible decisions without unnecessary dependence on others. It does not require rejecting all cooperation or help.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: What does the expression "For a country to develop, a sound economic system is crucial" imply?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: simply take into consideration the economic potential

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: mobilize the existing resource in the country for genuine development.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: take into consideration exclusively the global economy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: merely take into consideration the manpower resource

explanation.solution_text_en: A sound economic system organizes and mobilizes a country's human, natural and financial resources for productive and sustainable development. Focusing on only one resource or only the global economy is too narrow.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 6 & 7: Economic Development; Sectors and Strategies

questions.question_text_en: What do we mean by "Improving one's own skill is imperative to stay competitive"?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: You do not need to adapt to new technologies

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: If we fail to learn, we may not easily survive the struggle in life.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Operating mobile phones are not as such important

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Operating television and radio is adequate

explanation.solution_text_en: Skills must be updated as technology and work change. Continuous learning improves adaptability and employability, while refusing to learn makes it harder to remain competitive.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Grade 11 Economics - human capital/development

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following demonstrates the characteristics of a self-reliant person? He/she is one who
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: has good social skills such as sharing materials, ideas and ask for help.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: looks down on menial jobs.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: lacks confidence and the spirit of hard work.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: envies his/her friends when they score good results.

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-reliance is compatible with cooperation, sharing ideas and asking for appropriate help. A self-reliant person is confident and responsible, not contemptuous of work, envious or passive.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a characteristic of a dependent person?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Courage to criticize others.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Inconsistent in action and decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Initiative for general welfare.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ability to be dependable.

explanation.solution_text_en: A dependent person often lacks consistency and confidence in making and carrying out decisions without excessive reliance on others. Initiative and dependability are positive traits associated with responsibility and self-reliance.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Kidist is a university student who leads her life by planning. Which of the following activities relates to Kidist?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: She is extravagant

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: She lacks time for study

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: She lacks money to save

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: She sets priorities for her activities

explanation.solution_text_en: Planning requires setting priorities, organizing time and allocating resources according to goals. Extravagance and chronic shortages of time or money usually signal weak planning.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Grade 11 Economics - Consumption and Saving

questions.question_text_en: Abebe is a grade ten student. He has two sisters and two brothers. His family size is seven. His mother is a housewife while his father is a government employee. Which of the following is true about Abebe's family?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The facts given are insufficient to prove that the family's income and size are incompatible because the father's actual income, assets and other resources are not stated. A is the intended/closest answer, not a certain inference.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Its income and size of family are incompatible

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It sets goals and lead its life accordingly

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It has a family planning based on its income and budget

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It does not need family planning and budget

explanation.solution_text_en: The item appears to intend the conclusion that a relatively large household supported by one stated wage earner may face pressure between income and family size. Sound family budgeting should instead be based on actual income, needs and resources.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - household consumption, saving and budgeting

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following describes the importance of social and political participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Being elected as a representative of people and advance your own interest.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Can lobbying government officials to solve community problems.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Participating in youth associations to primarily benefit your own self.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Being elected as representative of people and back only your political party

explanation.solution_text_en: Social and political participation is valuable when citizens use lawful channels to address community problems and influence public decisions. Lobbying officials for community needs is a clear example of such participation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Obang has a good skill of using information. Which of the following is true about Obang?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: He has a talent and skill to get information with no skill of using it.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: He has the knowledge of the sources of information but does not know how to use it.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: He is not familiar with the sources of information and how to use it.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: He has the ability to find, evaluate, analyze and arrange information

explanation.solution_text_en: Information literacy involves locating information, judging its reliability, analyzing it and organizing it for responsible use. Knowing sources without evaluating or using them is incomplete.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 2: Culture of Using Digital Technology; Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: An idea or thought that comes from the analysis of facts is known as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Information

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Knowledge

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Wisdom

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Concept

explanation.solution_text_en: Knowledge is developed when facts and information are analyzed and understood so that they form meaningful ideas or conclusions. Wisdom goes further by applying knowledge with sound judgment.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which of one of the following is the importance of truthfulness?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is the quality of truthless individuals

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It makes you become mistrusted by others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It helps you to earn reputation from others

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Enable us to hide our wrong doings

explanation.solution_text_en: Truthfulness builds trust and a good reputation because others can rely on what a truthful person says and does. Lying or hiding wrongdoing has the opposite effect.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following actions helps to minimize extravagant practices?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Avoiding buying things

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Buying things for no reason

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Fixing a budget before shopping

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Avoiding any social ceremonies which require money

explanation.solution_text_en: A budget helps a person distinguish needs from wants, set spending limits and avoid impulsive purchases. Avoiding every purchase or every social event is neither necessary nor realistic.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Consumption, Saving and Investment

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements defines best planning?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is to systematically use available resources so as to achieve our goal

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It is the ability to face something we didn't intend

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is to work out what we need to do in order to achieve unintended goal

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is the ability to do something which is not carefully organized

explanation.solution_text_en: Planning is the organized use of time, money and other resources to reach intended goals. The other choices describe unplanned or unintended action.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: One of the following statements summarizes the role of civic societies.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: They do not interfere in the affairs of government

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: They work to mobilize youth for active participation for progress

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: They are organization which do not manifest the will of citizens

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: They only represent the voiceless segments of the society

explanation.solution_text_en: Civil-society organizations can educate and mobilize citizens, create forums for participation and contribute to social progress. Their role is broader than representing only one category of people.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statement describes the necessity of knowledge in society?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Knowledge may not help a given society to creatively solve its problems

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Knowledge mainly serves to understand what exists outside a given society

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Knowledge benefits only the individual who acquires it

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Knowledge requires an inclusive society to serve as a key resource for development

explanation.solution_text_en: Knowledge becomes a development resource when people across society can create, share and apply it to solve problems. It is not useful only to the individual who possesses it.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: Abebe is renowned for his strict adherence to truth; as he
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: is honest and not telling any lies

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: scrutinizes rules which he thinks are untruthful

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: always fight against layers

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: is open-minded to listen to lies

explanation.solution_text_en: Strict adherence to truth is honesty: speaking truthfully and avoiding deliberate lies or deception. This is a core ethical value.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains best the indivisibility of rights?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: None of the options defines indivisibility perfectly. A stronger statement would say that civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights are all important and mutually reinforcing.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The right to prosper is respected without respecting the right to property.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Human rights and democratic rights are independent from each other.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The prevalence of democratic rights ensures the respect of human rights.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The different rights stated in the constitution are unrelated to each other

explanation.solution_text_en: Human rights are interdependent and indivisible: progress in one group of rights often supports the enjoyment of others. Among the choices, C best expresses this linkage between democratic and human rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes best the importance of tolerance for multicultural Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: All Ethiopians need to have identical views

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: We have to be offended when we see the cultures of others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: We are irresponsible for the respect of rights of everyone

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It enables peaceful coexistence among ethnic groups

explanation.solution_text_en: Tolerance allows people with different languages, cultures, religions and identities to live together peacefully and with mutual respect. It does not require everyone to hold identical views.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about the democratization process in Ethiopia since the 20th century?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: More than one option contains a historically true element. The Derg was also repressive, and student movements did challenge the imperial government. D is selected because it most directly matches the curriculum narrative of the late imperial period.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The recurrence of student uprisings exposed Emperor Haile Selassie's repressive regime to the outside world.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Derg was notorious for its repression and bloody rule that enabled it to stay in power.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Emperor Haile Selassie was able to meet people's demand for freedom and democracy.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Emperor Haile Selassie's autocratic rule made the situation in Ethiopia worse.

explanation.solution_text_en: Current history teaching describes imperial Ethiopia as facing growing demands for freedom and improved living conditions, with autocratic rule and repression contributing to mounting unrest before 1974. That makes D the most direct statement.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6: Ethiopia 1941-1991

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia has signed a number of international conventions and agreements. Which of the following explains the importance of signing the conventions and agreements?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's sovereignty is being compromised

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It spoils the cultures and values of Ethiopia

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It helps Ethiopia to attract foreign investments

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It threatens Ethiopian internal peace and security

explanation.solution_text_en: Participation in international conventions can strengthen legal certainty, cooperation and confidence between states, which can support trade and investment. The other options describe negative effects that do not follow simply from signing agreements.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Foreign Relations; Grade 11 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia has diplomats in many countries of the world. These diplomats are working to boost the Ethiopian foreign relations. What is the importance of boosting the foreign relations for Ethiopian development?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a foreign country to assure its national interests in the global arena.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ethiopia to assure its national interests in the global arena.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ethiopia to import a foreign country's dressing styles.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the foreign countries to protect their own interest and benefits.

explanation.solution_text_en: Diplomacy and foreign relations are tools for protecting and advancing Ethiopia's national interests - including peace, trade, investment and development - in the international arena.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa

questions.question_text_en: There are negative consequences of dependency. It paralyzes the self-esteem, self-confidence of individuals and economic progress, sovereignty of nations. Based on these facts, one can conclude that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: we can avoid its bad consequences.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: minimizing the nature of dependency and cultivating reciprocal contributions can normalize the negative impacts of dependency.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: by a voiding dependent people, we can establish a society with good self-esteem and national strength

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: since dependency is natural, we change its negative consequences.

explanation.solution_text_en: The goal is not to isolate dependent people but to reduce harmful dependence and build reciprocal, capacity-enhancing relationships. Mutual contribution and stronger self-reliance can reduce the negative effects of dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: To effectively fight contraband, governments need to collaborate with citizens. In such cooperation, while citizens are expected to understand its consequences and know their responsibilities, governments can
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: close all the borders where there are susceptible contrabandists.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: institutionalize contraband in a way that government can take its shares from the income.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: ban contraband by law and take proper measures when it is committed.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: promote local products and avoid foreign products in the market.

explanation.solution_text_en: Government has a duty to prohibit contraband through law and enforce those laws fairly, while citizens cooperate by understanding the harm and reporting or avoiding illegal trade. Closing every border is neither practical nor necessary.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance; Grade 11 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: Identify the statement that explains best the relationship between money, capital and world politics in financing development effort in a country.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Funding policies of international monetary organizations must be based on the principles and demands of the developing countries.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The developed countries use international monetary institutions to assume political and cultural leadership of developing countries.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Developed countries use international monetary institutions to meet the national political objectives of the developing countries.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: International monetary organizations give loans and grants when developing countries satisfy some specified conditions.

explanation.solution_text_en: International financial institutions commonly attach policy, repayment or program conditions to loans and grants. This shows how development finance can be connected with wider policy and political considerations.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 5: Trade and Finance; Unit 6: Economic Development

questions.question_text_en: The study of the behaviors of individual agents, analysis of particular group of people is not enough. We need to understand and comprehend the cumulative picture of what goes on in the economy. Doing so is the paradigm of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: microeconomics

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: macroeconomics

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: mesoeconomics

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: both micro and macroeconomics

explanation.solution_text_en: Macroeconomics studies economy-wide outcomes such as total output, inflation, unemployment and aggregate spending. Microeconomics focuses more on individual consumers, firms and specific markets.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 1: Fundamental Concepts of Macroeconomics

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is not a proper and legitimate role of associations in civic participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Mobilize and ignite citizens for political transition.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Serve as forums to analyze the problems of the community.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Help extensively in the participation of citizens in policy making.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Better access to analyze the information about the problems of the people.

explanation.solution_text_en: Civic associations properly provide forums, information, advocacy and participation around public issues. Mobilizing citizens specifically for a political transition moves beyond the ordinary non-partisan civic role described by the curriculum.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Mr. John is a leader, who utilizes motivation. This means that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: he uses powerful words to force workers.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: he engages in mobilizing workers by innovative mechanisms.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: he mobilizes workers to support him in assuming leadership position.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: he devises his own laws that guide the organizational activities.

explanation.solution_text_en: Motivation means encouraging people to contribute willingly by using incentives, communication, recognition and creative leadership methods. Forcing workers or inventing personal laws is not motivation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values / responsible leadership

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements explains what reasoning and objectivity mean?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Objectivity is a process of thought that helps to make reasonable judgment

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Reasoning and objectivity are incompatible components of knowledge and judgments

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: When knowledge and objective put together, they can give rise to reasonable judgment

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Reasoning is a process of thought that helps to make objective judgment

explanation.solution_text_en: Reasoning is the thinking process used to examine evidence and reach justified conclusions; good reasoning supports objective judgment. Objectivity is the quality of judging on evidence rather than bias.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: While we gather information from different sources like media, public discussions, books, personal experiences and observations, proper use of information as an outcome of interpretation and analysis is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: to shape public visions in the government and its organizations so as to foster the success of parties.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: to mobilize the audiences towards prescribed goals of particular groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: to advance knowledge and enhance our practical capabilities to act in certain manner that enrich common good.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: to differentiate supporters and opponents and set one's proper mechanism of dismissing opponents.

explanation.solution_text_en: Responsible use of information should expand knowledge and practical capacity in ways that serve the common good. Manipulating audiences or excluding opponents is inconsistent with ethical citizenship and media literacy.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 2: Digital Technology; Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is correct about payment of tax and tax payers?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Everyone as a legal citizen is responsible to pay taxes since he/she is benefiting from public services.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Any citizen who has an income that satisfies minimum requirement of responsibilities is to pay tax.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Everyone who has an income for his/her subsistence should pay tax since tax is a portion of one's income.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Business men/women are more responsible to pay tax because the amount of tax is more preferable by the government.

explanation.solution_text_en: Tax liability depends on the law, including the tax base and applicable thresholds. Not every citizen must pay every tax, but people with taxable income or transactions that meet legal requirements are responsible for payment.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which statement shows the advantages and disadvantages of parliamentary and presidential systems of government?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: In a presidential system, the president heads the executive branch and the legislative one and this gives the system a power to check and balance.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Since enacting laws is easier in a presidential system of government than in a parliamentary system, adopting presidential system is better than parliamentary system.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: In a parliamentary system since the Prime Minster is the head of the executive and the member of the legislative branch, it weakens the possibility of checks and balances.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: In a presidential system of government, the president has the power to make treaties with other nations with his/her freedom of practicing according to the treaty.

explanation.solution_text_en: In parliamentary systems the executive is formed from, and normally depends on, the legislature; this can reduce the strict separation of powers compared with a presidential system. Whether that is an advantage or disadvantage depends on institutional design, but C states the recognized structural trade-off most accurately.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - democracy/government institutions; Grade 9 - constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: Among the basic principle of the Ethiopian constitution, the one which vests power on nations, nationalities and people of Ethiopia is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the supremacy of the government

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: accountability of the government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: separation of state and religion

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the sovereignty of the people

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE Constitution states that sovereign power resides in the Nations, Nationalities and Peoples of Ethiopia. Government authority is therefore derived from the people rather than from officials themselves.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 5; FDRE Constitution Art. 8

questions.question_text_en: Helen is a member of an advocacy group which gives awareness for citizens about their constitutional rights and responsibilities. On one occasion, her team held discussion with a group of workers who demanded a salary increment and threatened to seize factory property till their demand is met. Instead, she advised them to demand their rights in an appropriate way without abandoning their duties. This case demonstrates that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: rights and responsibility must be kept in balance.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: absence from duty is justified so long as demands are not met.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: rights more important than responsibility

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: one must demand his/her rights by all means.

explanation.solution_text_en: Citizens should claim rights through lawful and peaceful means while also respecting the rights of others and fulfilling legitimate responsibilities. Rights and responsibilities therefore operate together in democratic citizenship.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statement is correct about accountability of government?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The police are denied to use violence even in dangerous conditions.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Some members of the executive are not obliged to follow the law of the land.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: To make office bearer actions opens to be inspected.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To hold officials responsible for wrong doings.
