explanation.solution_text_en: Accountability means that officials can be required to explain their actions and can be held responsible for wrongdoing or failure in public duties. Openness to inspection is closely related transparency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Understanding Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Article 51 sub article 2 of the Ethiopian constitution, says all powers not given exclusively to the federal government and the states are reserved to
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The question cites Article 51(2), but the residual-powers rule is in Article 52(1) of the FDRE Constitution. The substantive answer is still B: the States.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the republic president

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the state

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the prime minister

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the federal

explanation.solution_text_en: Residual powers - powers not expressly assigned to the federal government alone or concurrently - are reserved to the States. This is a key feature of the constitutional division of powers in Ethiopian federalism.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Art. 52(1)

questions.question_text_en: When rulers exercise unlimited power in a country, the outcome is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: upholding rule of law

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: absolute security

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: promotion of shared rule

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: deciding on matters as they wish

explanation.solution_text_en: Unlimited rulers are not effectively constrained by law or accountable institutions, so they can make decisions according to their own will. That is the opposite of rule of law and limited government.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following indicates the outcome of traditional conflict resolution mechanisms?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Respecting the laws of the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: End with a win-win solution

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Working jointly on common problems

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Sport activities

explanation.solution_text_en: Indigenous conflict-resolution mechanisms commonly emphasize reconciliation, restored relationships and settlements acceptable to both sides. A win-win outcome best captures that goal.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution

questions.question_text_en: Constitutionalism is the feature of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: fascist rule

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: unlimited government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: totalitarian rule

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: limited government

explanation.solution_text_en: Constitutionalism means government power is limited and exercised according to constitutional rules and rights. It is therefore a feature of limited government, not totalitarian or fascist rule.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: One of the following methods is appropriate to struggle against the act of injustice in the context of Ethiopian society?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Taking a case to the legal court to ensure one's rights.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Engaging in violent means against the suspected criminal.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Destroying the moral values of the wrongdoer.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Devaluing the informal laws of the society when they are to be used.

explanation.solution_text_en: A lawful way to challenge injustice is to use courts or other legitimate complaint and remedy mechanisms. Violence and personal retaliation undermine rule of law.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 3 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Among the following statements, one is correct regarding the concept of equality in terms of individual interest and public interest. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Individual interest is more important than public interest.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Equal protection of individuals is guaranteed so long as it has no adverse effect on public interest.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Equality implies getting whatever one wishes.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Individuals have the right to equality with a limitation.

explanation.solution_text_en: Equality protects individuals against unjust discrimination while recognizing that rights operate within a legal order that also protects the rights and legitimate interests of others and the public. Equal protection does not mean getting whatever one wishes.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Sharing responsibility in carrying out different activities fairly is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: equality of benefit

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: services

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: welfare

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: equality of burdens

explanation.solution_text_en: Equality of burdens means duties and costs are shared fairly according to relevant principles rather than imposed arbitrarily on only some members of society.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - good governance/equality; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following explains best the formulation of the 1995 FDRE's constitution?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: "Formulation" and "adoption" are different stages. The Constitutional Commission prepared the draft; the Constituent Assembly, which is not listed, adopted the Constitution.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the constitutional commission

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the House of Federation

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the parliament

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Nations and Nationalities

explanation.solution_text_en: The Constitutional Commission played the central role in preparing and formulating the draft that became the 1995 FDRE Constitution. The Constituent Assembly later debated and adopted the constitution.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 12 History - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: Your Civics and Ethical Education teacher told you that you need to abide yourself by the rule of law? What does he mean by this? You need to respect
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: your school director more than anyone else

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the law and act according to the law

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: government officials more than anyone else

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: all your teachers more than anyone else

explanation.solution_text_en: To abide by the rule of law means respecting the law and acting according to it. Rule of law does not require giving personal officials or school authorities greater respect than the law itself.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about equality after the transition to democracy in Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: All peoples of Ethiopia participate in decision making through their representatives.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: There is an absolute equality among all Nations, Nationalities and Peoples.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: All Nations, Nationalities and Peoples are receiving identical treatment and reward.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Few military leaders control political power in a highly centralized government.

explanation.solution_text_en: Representative participation is a central element of democratic equality: peoples and citizens take part in public decision-making directly or through chosen representatives. Equality does not require identical rewards or outcomes.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1; Grade 9 - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: Your Civics and Ethical Education teacher is teaching you about gender equality. After explaining what gender equality is all about, he told you that you have to respect gender equality at your home. What does he mean by that?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Boys are not supposed to work in the house

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The right place for girls is at home, not school

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Boys must help their sisters in the house

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Women are not capable of doing the job that men can do

explanation.solution_text_en: Gender equality at home requires sharing responsibilities without assuming that household work belongs only to girls or women. Boys helping their sisters with household tasks is the only option that moves toward equal responsibility.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is the importance of a fair distribution of social services?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It results in skirmish among people

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It improves the lives of people

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It benefits only some sections of the people

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It necessary to prohibit democracy

explanation.solution_text_en: Fair access to social services such as education, health and infrastructure improves wellbeing and expands opportunity. Unequal or exclusionary distribution can deepen social grievances.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 3 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Identify the true statement about the functions of courts under different political systems in Ethiopia.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: During the monarchical period, the Supreme Court was the last appellate court.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: During the Derg regime, cases which involve serious crimes were handled by first instance court.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: In a unitary system, both federal and regional government have their own judiciary system.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: In a federal system, issues of higher value which involve the federal government are seen by higher courts.

explanation.solution_text_en: Under the imperial court structure, the Supreme Imperial Court stood at the apex of the formal judiciary and served as the highest appellate court. The other options misstate features of unitary/federal judicial organization or court jurisdiction.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6; constitutional and justice-system context

questions.question_text_en: Identified the type of tax that is categorized under an indirect type of tax.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Value Added Tax

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Income Tax

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Business Profit Tax

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Rental Tax

explanation.solution_text_en: Value Added Tax is an indirect tax because it is collected through transactions on goods and services and can be passed through prices to consumers. Income, business-profit and rental-income taxes are direct taxes.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Admasu believes in the equality of all citizens. Which one of the following demonstrates best Admasu's behavior?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: He treats people with disabilities the same as his other friends

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: He respects some people over the others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: He overlooks the views of his friends

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: He want only boys, not girls, to come to school

explanation.solution_text_en: Belief in equality is demonstrated by treating persons with disabilities with equal dignity and respect rather than excluding them. Equality also supports reasonable measures that enable full participation where needed.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: What is the difference between the idea of chauvinism and warmonger?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Chauvinism refers to having irrational belief in superiority of dominance of one's own people unlike warmonger.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Warmonger stands for showing aggressive patriotism unlike chauvinism.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Chauvinism refers to promoting aggressions towards other group unlike warmonger.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Warmonger refers to having excessive nationalism intended to dominate others unlike chauvinism.

explanation.solution_text_en: Chauvinism is excessive or irrational belief in the superiority of one's own nation or group. A warmonger is someone who promotes or encourages war; the concepts can overlap, but they are not the same.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Grade 9 - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: As a student, which one of the following demonstrates best your responsibilities?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2014/2015 E.C. Booklet 271

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Studying hard only not helping your family

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Disrespecting the viewpoints of your classmates

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Taking part in an activity which contributes to the good of the society

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Not participating actively outside of the school

explanation.solution_text_en: Students have responsibilities beyond personal study, including constructive participation in family, school and community life. Taking part in activities that contribute to society is a clear example of active citizenship.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization; Unit 7: Patriotism
